sop_modules.name: Exterior Door Protection & Equipment Setup
sop_modules.description: Deploy entry walkway protection, remove door hardware (labeled bags, photograph before removal), protect weatherstripping (pull out friction-fit or deep-tape non-removable), mask glass lites (panel/grand_entry doors), protect threshold, set up spray or brush equipment. Hardware is REMOVED per doctrine — not masked. Areas beneath hardware must be sealed.

tasks.name: Entry Walkway/Porch Protection
tasks.description: Deploy canvas drop cloths over entry walkway, porch, and stoop area below door work zone. Non-slip canvas for crew traffic. For spray application: extend plastic sheeting to overspray containment zone.

quality_notes.all: Canvas for crew traffic on porch/stoop. Plastic extension for spray overspray zone. Secure against wind.

tasks.name: Door Hardware Removal
tasks.description: Remove ALL door hardware: lockset, deadbolt, strike plates, hinges, address numbers, knocker, mail slot, doorbell. Photograph hardware layout BEFORE removal. Place each door's hardware in labeled ziplock bag with door location and contents. Areas beneath hardware must be sealed during prime/finish to prevent moisture infiltration. Grand entry may have 2+ hardware groups.

quality_notes.QT3: Full hardware removal. Photograph layout. Labeled bags.
quality_notes.QT4: Full hardware removal. Photograph layout. Labeled bags. Inspect hinge mortises for defects to fill.
quality_notes.QT5: Full hardware removal. Photograph layout. Labeled bags. Inspect all mortises. Document hinge alignment marks for precision reinstall.

tasks.name: Weatherstrip Protection
tasks.description: Protect weatherstripping from paint contact. Friction-fit stripping: gently pull out, store safely for re-insert after finish dries. Non-removable stripping: push low-tack tape deep into gap between jamb and stripping with putty knife. NEVER paint weatherstripping — destroys elasticity, causes brittleness and seal tearing.

quality_notes.all: Verify stripping is fully protected or removed before any prime/finish work. No paint on stripping material.

tasks.name: Threshold/Sill Protection
tasks.description: Apply tape and plastic film over door threshold/sill to catch drips during door edge and face painting. Especially critical during bottom edge painting. Extend protection to door swing arc on interior side.

quality_notes.all: Complete threshold coverage. Extend to interior floor at door swing.

tasks.name: Glass Lite Masking
tasks.description: Mask all glass lites in door slab and sidelites/transom (grand_entry). Apply exterior-grade UV-resistant tape (14-day minimum) at glass-to-frame edge, then apply HDPE static-cling masking film over glass area. Grand entry with sidelites and transom requires significantly more masking time. This spec owns glass masking when painting the DOOR itself — distinct from trim spec which masks glass adjacent to CASING.

quality_notes.QT3: Complete glass coverage. Tape sealed tight to frame edge.
quality_notes.QT4: Complete glass coverage. Tape sealed tight. Inspect for bleed-through potential at edges.
quality_notes.QT5: Liquid mask alternative for razor-sharp paint lines at glass edge. Complete coverage with premium edge definition.

tasks.name: Spray Equipment Setup
tasks.description: Configure airless sprayer with door-specific tips: 310 tip (0.010 inch orifice, 6-inch fan) for steel/fiberglass faces, 411 tip (0.011 inch, 8-inch fan) for wood faces. Install 60-mesh black filter for latex. Stage angled sash brush (2.5 inch) for panel recesses and edge work. Stage flat brush (2 inch) for narrow edge painting.

quality_notes.all: Verify tip size matches substrate. Test spray pattern on cardboard before door application. Stage brush for edge/detail work.

tasks.name: Brush Equipment Setup
tasks.description: Stage brushes: angled sash brush (2.5 inch) for faces, panel recesses, and detail work. Flat brush (2 inch) for narrow edges. Paint pots and materials. Set up access equipment per access_type (typically ground level for entry doors, ladder for elevated entries).

quality_notes.all: Verify access equipment stability. Stage materials within reach of working position.

sop_modules.sequence_notes: Walkway protection first -> Hardware removal -> Weatherstrip protection -> Threshold protection -> Glass masking (if applicable) -> Equipment setup last.

sop_modules.name: Exterior Door Surface Preparation
sop_modules.description: Substrate-driven preparation: Steel = solvent clean (xylene/acetone) + TSP wash + degloss 120-150 grit + dent fill (if needed). Fiberglass = mild soap wash + light scuff 220 on paint-grade smooth (do NOT sand textured grain). Wood = sand 120-150 grit + fill defects + tannin spot prime knots + caulk panel joints. Tasks activate based on substrate_material and substrate_state.

tasks.name: Solvent Clean Steel Door
tasks.description: Wipe all steel door surfaces with xylene or acetone to remove manufacturing oils, release agents, waxes, and silicone contaminants. Wipe test with clean white rag to verify decontamination. Follow with TSP detergent wash and rinse.

substrate_state_rules.notes: Bare steel requires full solvent clean to remove manufacturing contaminants.
Factory-primed steel still needs surface decontamination before topcoat.
Field-primed surface was cleaned before priming.

quality_notes.all: Full solvent wipe. White rag verification — no color transfer = clean. CRITICAL: bare ferrous metal must be primed same day as prep.

site_condition_rules.notes: NEVER use hydrocarbon solvents on fiberglass — damages resin matrix.

tasks.name: Degloss/Scuff Sand Steel Door
tasks.description: Light sand steel door surfaces with 120-150 grit to degloss existing factory primer and create mechanical tooth for topcoat adhesion. Feather scratches and minor rust spots with 300-grit until transition is imperceptible.

substrate_state_rules.notes: Bare steel: sand to remove light oxidation and create profile.
Factory primer: scuff-sand to degloss for topcoat adhesion.
Field-primed surface was prepped before priming.

quality_notes.QT3: Even scuff pattern. No glossy patches remaining.
quality_notes.QT4: Full surface sand. Feather all scratches to imperceptible transition.
quality_notes.QT5: Systematic sand with raking light inspection. Zero visible scratch marks. Feather all imperfections to 300-grit smooth.

tasks.name: Steel Door Dent Repair
tasks.description: Sand dented area with 80-grit. Apply two-component auto body filler. Shape and finish-sand with 240/300-grit until flush with surrounding surface. Per Exterior_Doors_Doctrine.md section 2.

quality_notes.QT3: Fill visible dents. Flush finish.
quality_notes.QT4: Fill all dents and dings. Sand to smooth flush. Raking light verify.
quality_notes.QT5: Fill ALL imperfections including minor surface waviness. Perfect flush finish. DFT-compatible fill depth.

tasks.name: Wash Fiberglass Door
tasks.description: Clean fiberglass door surfaces with mild dish soap or denatured alcohol. NEVER use hydrocarbon-based solvents (xylene, acetone, mineral spirits) — damages fiberglass resin matrix. Rinse thoroughly and allow to dry completely before priming.

substrate_state_rules.notes: Factory-primed fiberglass needs washing before topcoat.

quality_notes.all: Mild soap only. NO hydrocarbon solvents. Rinse completely. Dry before next step.

tasks.name: Light Scuff Sand Fiberglass Door (Paint-Grade Only)
tasks.description: Light scuff sand paint-grade (smooth) fiberglass door with 220-grit to create mechanical adhesion profile. Do NOT sand textured (stain-grade) fiberglass — destroys the wood-grain profile. Only scuff smooth paint-grade surfaces.

substrate_state_rules.notes: Scuff factory primer on smooth fiberglass for topcoat adhesion.

quality_notes.all: LIGHT scuff only on smooth/paint-grade fiberglass. Do NOT sand textured stain-grade — destroys wood-grain profile.

tasks.name: Sand Wood Door
tasks.description: Sand all wood door surfaces (both faces, all 4 edges, frame/jamb) with 120-150 grit. Remove mill glaze, open wood grain for primer adhesion. Hand sand panel recesses and profiles. Orbital sander for flat face areas.

substrate_state_rules.notes: New bare wood requires full sanding to remove mill glaze and open grain.
Factory-primed wood was sanded before priming.

quality_notes.QT3: Full surface sand. Even scratch pattern. No glossy patches.
quality_notes.QT4: Full surface sand with systematic coverage. Inspect all edges.
quality_notes.QT5: Full systematic sand with raking light inspection. All surfaces including panel recesses and end grain.

tasks.name: Fill Wood Door Defects
tasks.description: Fill nail holes, minor defects, and small damage on wood door surfaces with exterior-rated wood filler. Allow to cure per manufacturer spec. Sand flush with 150-220 grit.

substrate_state_rules.notes: New wood doors may have minor defects, machining marks, nail holes.

quality_notes.QT3: Fill visible defects. Sand flush.
quality_notes.QT4: Fill all defects > 1/16 inch. Sand flush. Verify with raking light.
quality_notes.QT5: Fill ALL defects > 1/32 inch. Glazing putty for micro-imperfections. Perfect flush finish.

tasks.name: Tannin Knot Spot Prime (Wood)
tasks.description: Spot-apply alkyd or shellac-based stain-blocking primer to visible knots on tannin-rich wood species (mahogany, cedar, redwood, Douglas fir). Brush apply to individual knots BEFORE full acrylic primer coat. Prevents tannin bleed staining through finish coat.

substrate_state_rules.notes: Tannin-rich bare wood species need spot prime on knots.

quality_notes.QT3: Spot prime visible knots. Complete seal over each knot.
quality_notes.QT4: Spot prime all knots including small ones. Extended coverage around knot area.
quality_notes.QT5: Spot prime all knots with extended perimeter coverage. Verify seal after drying — re-coat if bleed-through visible.

tasks.name: Caulk Wood Panel Joints
tasks.description: Apply flexible paintable caulk to wood door panel joints to seal gaps and prevent moisture infiltration. Use exterior-rated acrylic latex caulk. Allow full cure before painting. NOTE: casing-to-wall caulking is SF_TRIM_EXT_NC_v1 scope, not this spec.

quality_notes.QT3: Caulk visible gaps at panel joints. Clean tooled bead.
quality_notes.QT4: Caulk all panel joints. Uniform bead. Clean tool lines.
quality_notes.QT5: Caulk all joints with precision tooling. Zero visible caulk ridges after sanding. Allow full cure per sealant type.

tasks.name: Dust Removal After Prep
tasks.description: Remove all sanding dust from door surfaces, panel recesses, edges, and frame using tack cloth. Ensure zero dust contamination before primer or finish application.

quality_notes.all: Complete dust removal including panel recesses and edge rabbets. White-glove test for QT5.

sop_modules.sequence_notes: Substrate-specific cleaning first (solvent clean steel, wash fiberglass) -> Mechanical prep (degloss/sand) -> Fill defects -> Tannin spot prime (wood only) -> Caulk panel joints -> Final dust removal.

sop_modules.name: Exterior Door Primer Application
sop_modules.description: Substrate-driven primer: DTM primer for bare steel (SYS_EXT_DOOR_PRIMER_DTM), 100% acrylic primer for fiberglass/wood (SYS_EXT_DOOR_PRIMER_ACRYLIC). Skip for factory-primed steel/fiberglass with good adhesion (SS_EXT_PRIMED_FACTORY) and field-primed (SS_EXT_PRIMED_FIELD). Wood doors get six-side seal primer on all surfaces including top/bottom edges. CRITICAL: bare ferrous metal MUST be primed same day as surface prep.

tasks.name: Spray DTM Primer — Steel Door Faces
tasks.description: Apply DTM (Direct-to-Metal) primer to steel door faces using airless sprayer with 310 tip. Rust-inhibitive pigments provide sacrificial barrier protection. CRITICAL: prime same day as surface prep — bare ferrous metal begins rusting within hours. Even, wet coat per manufacturer mil spec.

substrate_state_rules.notes: Bare steel requires DTM primer. Must prime same day as prep.
Factory-primed steel with good adhesion skips field prime.

quality_notes.all: Even wet coat. No holidays. Same-day prime after prep. Target 1.5 mils DFT.

tasks.name: Brush DTM Primer — Steel Door (Faces/Edges)
tasks.description: Apply DTM primer to steel door faces and all 4 edges by brush. Used when spray is not available or for small projects. Same DTM chemistry as spray. Brush provides better control on edges and panel details.

quality_notes.all: Even coat, no drips. Same-day prime after prep. Complete coverage of faces and all 4 edges.

tasks.name: Spray Acrylic Primer — Fiberglass/Wood Door Faces
tasks.description: Apply 100% acrylic latex exterior primer to fiberglass or wood door faces using airless sprayer. 411 tip for wood, 310 for fiberglass. Acrylic primer is MANDATORY for fiberglass — oil-based/alkyd prohibited due to outgassing blister risk. For wood: covers all six sides (both faces, all 4 edges, frame/jamb).

substrate_state_rules.notes: Bare wood and unprimed fiberglass require full primer coat.
Factory-primed fiberglass/wood with good adhesion skips field prime.

quality_notes.all: Even wet coat. No holidays. 100% acrylic ONLY on fiberglass — no oil/alkyd.

tasks.name: Brush Acrylic Primer — Fiberglass/Wood Door (Faces/Edges)
tasks.description: Apply 100% acrylic latex exterior primer to fiberglass or wood door faces, all 4 edges, and frame/jamb by brush. Angled sash for faces and panel recesses, flat brush for narrow edges. 100% acrylic MANDATORY for fiberglass.

quality_notes.all: Even coat. No drips. Complete six-side coverage for wood. 100% acrylic ONLY on fiberglass.

tasks.name: Prime All Door Edges
tasks.description: Brush prime all 4 door edges (top, bottom, hinge, latch) with substrate-appropriate primer. This task runs in addition to face priming when faces are sprayed — edges are always brushed regardless of face method. Bottom edge is critical moisture entry point on wood doors. Prop door open during bottom edge cure.

quality_notes.all: Complete edge coverage including top and bottom. Prop door open during bottom edge dry. No drips or sags on vertical edges.

tasks.name: Six-Side Seal Verification (Wood)
tasks.description: Verify that all six sides of wood door have received primer: both faces, top edge, bottom edge, hinge edge, latch edge. Bottom edge is the primary moisture entry point — unsealed end-grain causes massive wicking and swelling. Prop door open during cure to prevent bottom seal sticking. Failure to seal = warranty voidance.

substrate_state_rules.notes: All bare wood doors require six-side seal verification.

quality_notes.QT3: Visual verify all 6 sides primed. Bottom edge confirmed.
quality_notes.QT4: Flashlight inspect all edges. Mirror for bottom edge. Confirm no holidays.
quality_notes.QT5: Full six-side inspection with mirror and raking light. DFT spot-check on primer coat.

sop_modules.sequence_notes: DTM primer for steel faces -> Acrylic primer for fiberglass/wood faces -> Edge priming (spray method: separate edge task) -> Six-side seal verification (wood only). CRITICAL: bare metal — prime same day as prep.

sop_modules.name: Exterior Door First Finish Coat
sop_modules.description: First finish coat application. Spray door faces for factory-smooth quality (primary method), brush panel recesses and all 4 edges. Back-rolling AVOIDED on metal doors — introduces orange peel. Paneled doors: brush recesses first (panels, then stiles, then rails), then spray/brush faces, then brush edges. Standard or premium acrylic enamel per quality tier; IR-reflective mandatory for LRV < 30.

tasks.name: Spray First Finish Coat — Door Faces
tasks.description: Spray first finish coat on both door faces using airless sprayer. 310 tip for steel/fiberglass, 411 tip for wood. Even wet coat, maintain wet edge, uniform mil build. Do NOT back-roll on metal doors — orange peel is undesirable. For panel doors: spray flat panel areas between brushed recesses.

quality_notes.QT3: Even coat, no runs or sags. Clean edges.
quality_notes.QT4: Even coat with premium material. Inspect for holidays, runs, sags before tipping off.
quality_notes.QT5: Spray in controlled environment (door removed to shop/garage). Fine tip pattern. Even wet film.

tasks.name: Brush First Finish Coat — Door Faces
tasks.description: Brush first finish coat on both door faces using angled sash brush (2.5 inch). For projects where spray setup is not justified. Brush technique: long even strokes following grain (wood) or vertical strokes (steel/fiberglass). Maintain wet edge to avoid lap marks.

quality_notes.QT3: Even coat, no lap marks. Clean edges.
quality_notes.QT4: Even coat with premium material. Tip off brush marks while wet.
quality_notes.QT5: Brush technique for zero visible marks. Long even strokes. May use foam pad for final tipping.

tasks.name: Brush Panel Recesses — First Finish Coat
tasks.description: Brush finish coat into panel recesses on raised panel doors. Work sequence: recessed panels first, then stiles (middle, top, center, bottom), then horizontal rails. Prevents lap marks and ensures complete coverage in panel profiles. Angled sash brush (2.5 inch or smaller) for recess detail.

quality_notes.QT3: Complete recess coverage. No puddles in corners.
quality_notes.QT4: Complete coverage. Thin even coat in recesses. No buildup at panel-to-stile transition.
quality_notes.QT5: Precision brush work in all recesses. Zero buildup, zero holidays. Raking light verify before dry.

tasks.name: Brush All Door Edges — First Finish Coat
tasks.description: Brush first finish coat on all 4 door edges (top, bottom, hinge, latch) using flat brush (2 inch). Edges are ALWAYS brushed regardless of face application method. Bottom edge: apply paint, prop door open during cure to prevent sticking. Hinge edge: complete coverage in hinge mortises.

quality_notes.QT3: Complete edge coverage. No drips on faces.
quality_notes.QT4: Complete coverage including hinge mortises. Clean edge-to-face transition.
quality_notes.QT5: Full edge coverage. Hinge mortises. Edge-to-face blend. Prop door for bottom edge cure.

tasks.name: Brush Mullions/Sidelite Frames — First Finish Coat
tasks.description: Brush first finish coat on sidelite and transom mullions, muntin bars, and frame sections on grand entry assemblies. Detailed brush work — tight profiles between glass lites. Angled sash brush for mullion detail.

quality_notes.QT3: Complete mullion coverage. Clean glass-to-mullion line.
quality_notes.QT4: Precision mullion work. No paint on glass. Sharp lines at masking edge.
quality_notes.QT5: Exacting mullion detail. Razor-sharp lines. Uniform film build on all profiles.

sop_modules.sequence_notes: Panel recesses (brush) first -> Faces (spray or brush) -> Edges (brush) -> Mullions/sidelites (grand_entry only, brush).

sop_modules.name: Exterior Door Intercoat Inspection & Sand
sop_modules.description: Between-coat inspection and maintenance. QT3: visual inspect only — no intercoat sanding. QT4: light scuff sand with 220-grit, dust removal. QT5: hand-sand with raking light inspection, 220/320-grit, address any runs/sags/holidays. Runs between finish coat 1 and finish coat 2.
sop_modules.run_rule: Runs AFTER first finish coat, BEFORE second finish coat. 1 interstage pass for 2-finish-coat system.

tasks.name: Intercoat Inspection
tasks.description: Inspect first finish coat for runs, sags, drips, holidays, orange peel, dust nibs, and coverage uniformity. Mark defects for repair. QT3: visual scan. QT4: raking light inspection. QT5: raking light + DFT spot check.

quality_notes.QT3: Visual scan for obvious defects — runs, sags, holidays.
quality_notes.QT4: Raking light inspection. Mark all defects. Check panel recesses for buildup.
quality_notes.QT5: Raking light + DFT gauge spot-check. Zero tolerance for runs, sags, or holidays. Document findings.

tasks.name: Intercoat Sand
tasks.description: Light scuff sand between finish coats to promote intercoat adhesion and remove minor defects. QT3: NOT performed — visual inspect only. QT4: light sand with 220-grit. QT5: hand-sand with 220/320-grit, feather any repaired areas.

quality_notes.QT4: Light scuff sand with 220-grit. Even scratch pattern. No aggressive sanding — just break gloss.
quality_notes.QT5: Hand-sand with 220-grit, finish with 320-grit in raking light. Feather all repairs to imperceptible transition.

tasks.name: Intercoat Defect Repair
tasks.description: Repair defects found during intercoat inspection: sand out runs/sags, spot-coat holidays, feather drip marks. For QT5: glazing putty for dust nibs.

quality_notes.QT4: Sand out runs/sags. Spot-coat holidays.
quality_notes.QT5: Full defect repair. Glazing putty for nibs. Feather all repairs. Re-inspect before coat 2.

tasks.name: Intercoat Dust Removal
tasks.description: Remove all sanding dust from door surfaces after intercoat sanding. Tack cloth all surfaces including panel recesses and edges. Ensure zero contamination before second finish coat.

quality_notes.all: Complete dust removal. Tack cloth all surfaces. White-glove verify for QT5.

sop_modules.sequence_notes: Allow recoat dry time per product spec -> Inspect -> Sand (QT4/QT5 only) -> Repair defects (if found) -> Dust removal -> Ready for coat 2.

sop_modules.name: Exterior Door Second Finish Coat
sop_modules.description: Second finish coat — same application method and technique as first coat. Doors ALWAYS get 2 finish coats regardless of quality tier (architectural focal point, exposed to weather). QT5: final coat may be applied with door hanging for gravity leveling on vertical faces.

tasks.name: Spray Second Finish Coat — Door Faces
tasks.description: Spray second finish coat on both door faces. Same technique as coat 1. QT5: final coat may be applied with door re-hung for gravity leveling — vertical spray for uniform film distribution.

quality_notes.QT3: Even coat, no runs or sags. Final visual.
quality_notes.QT4: Even coat with premium material. Raking light before dry.
quality_notes.QT5: Final coat. May spray with door hanging for gravity leveling. Zero defects.

tasks.name: Brush Second Finish Coat — Door Faces
tasks.description: Brush second finish coat on both door faces. Same technique as coat 1. Maintain wet edge, long even strokes.

quality_notes.QT3: Even coat, no lap marks.
quality_notes.QT4: Even coat. Tip off brush marks while wet.
quality_notes.QT5: Zero brush marks. Foam pad tipping for final smoothness.

tasks.name: Brush Panel Recesses — Second Finish Coat
tasks.description: Brush second finish coat into panel recesses. Same sequence as coat 1: panels first, stiles, then rails.

quality_notes.QT3: Complete recess coverage. No puddles.
quality_notes.QT4: Thin even coat. No buildup at transitions.
quality_notes.QT5: Precision detail. Zero buildup. Uniform film build.

tasks.name: Brush All Door Edges — Second Finish Coat
tasks.description: Brush second finish coat on all 4 door edges. Bottom edge: apply paint, prop door open during 24-48 hour cure to prevent bottom seal from sticking to threshold.

quality_notes.QT3: Complete edge coverage. Prop door for bottom edge cure.
quality_notes.QT4: Complete coverage. Clean transitions. Prop door.
quality_notes.QT5: Full edge coverage. Hinge mortises. Prop door 24-48 hrs.

tasks.name: Brush Mullions/Sidelite Frames — Second Finish Coat
tasks.description: Brush second finish coat on sidelite/transom mullions and frames. Same technique as coat 1.

quality_notes.QT3: Complete mullion coverage. Clean glass-to-mullion line.
quality_notes.QT4: Precision mullion work. Sharp masking lines.
quality_notes.QT5: Exacting detail. Razor-sharp lines. Uniform film.

sop_modules.sequence_notes: Panel recesses first -> Faces -> Edges -> Mullions. Same sequence as coat 1. Prop door open during bottom edge cure.

sop_modules.name: Exterior Door Hardware Reinstall & Weatherstrip
sop_modules.description: Reinstall all removed hardware using photographs as reference. Re-insert friction-fit weatherstripping. Test door operation — latching, locking, deadbolt engagement. Verify weatherseal compression. QT5: precision hinge alignment using documented marks.

tasks.name: Hardware Reinstallation
tasks.description: Reinstall all door hardware from labeled bags using pre-removal photographs as reference: lockset, deadbolt, strike plates, hinges, address numbers, knocker, mail slot, doorbell. Verify each component is correctly positioned and functional. Grand entry with additional hardware groups takes longer.

quality_notes.QT3: All hardware reinstalled. Correct positions. Functional test.
quality_notes.QT4: All hardware reinstalled. Verify alignment against photos. Full function test.
quality_notes.QT5: Precision reinstall using documented alignment marks. Full function test. Verify no paint contact on hardware finish.

tasks.name: Weatherstrip Reinstallation & Check
tasks.description: Re-insert friction-fit weatherstripping. Remove protective tape from non-removable stripping. Verify weatherseal compression around full door perimeter — door should close with slight resistance from stripping. Check for paint contamination on stripping and clean if found.

quality_notes.all: Stripping properly seated. Full perimeter compression. No paint contamination. Door seals evenly.

tasks.name: Door Operation Test
tasks.description: Test complete door operation: open/close smoothly, latch engages, deadbolt throws, strike plate alignment, no binding. Verify bottom edge clearance over threshold. Check that fresh paint on bottom edge is not contacting threshold during swing (prop door open if finish not fully cured).

quality_notes.QT3: Open/close. Latch. Deadbolt. No binding.
quality_notes.QT4: Full operation test. Verify alignment. Check bottom clearance.
quality_notes.QT5: Comprehensive operation test. Verify all hardware function. Bottom edge cure check. Door prop instructions to homeowner if not fully cured.

sop_modules.sequence_notes: Allow finish coat to cure per product spec (minimum touch-dry) -> Weatherstrip reinstall -> Hardware reinstall -> Operation test.

sop_modules.name: Exterior Door Final Inspection & Cleanup
sop_modules.description: Final visual inspection, touch-up of minor defects, glass masking removal, threshold protection teardown, walkway protection teardown, tool cleaning. QT5: DFT verification on finish coat.

tasks.name: Final Door Inspection
tasks.description: Final visual inspection of completed door: both faces, all 4 edges, panel recesses (if applicable), mullions (if grand_entry), glass masking lines. Mark any touch-up areas.

quality_notes.QT3: Visual scan for defects. Mark touch-ups.
quality_notes.QT4: Raking light inspection. All surfaces. Glass masking line quality.
quality_notes.QT5: Raking light + DFT verification (target 3.0-5.0 mils total system). Zero-defect standard. Document final DFT readings.

tasks.name: Touch-Up Minor Defects
tasks.description: Touch up minor defects found during final inspection: small holidays, edge drips, glass masking bleed-through. Brush touch-up with matching finish. Feather into surrounding area.

quality_notes.QT3: Address obvious defects.
quality_notes.QT4: Address all marked defects. Feather into surrounding.
quality_notes.QT5: Address every defect. Invisible feather. Re-inspect after touch-up.

tasks.name: Glass Masking Removal
tasks.description: Carefully remove glass masking film and tape from all glass lites, sidelites, and transom. Remove tape at angle to prevent paint film lifting. Clean any adhesive residue from glass. Inspect paint line quality at glass-to-frame edge.

quality_notes.QT3: Remove masking. Clean glass. Verify paint line.
quality_notes.QT4: Remove masking at angle. Clean adhesive residue. Sharp paint line.
quality_notes.QT5: Precision removal. Razor-clean glass. Razor-sharp paint line. Clean any micro-bleed with solvent.

tasks.name: Threshold Protection Teardown
tasks.description: Remove threshold tape and plastic protection. Clean any drips from threshold surface. Verify threshold finish is undamaged.

quality_notes.all: Clean removal. No adhesive residue on threshold. No paint drips remaining.

tasks.name: Walkway Protection Teardown
tasks.description: Remove canvas drop cloths and plastic sheeting from entry walkway/porch. Fold paint-side-in. Verify no paint drips on walkway surface.

quality_notes.all: Fold paint-side-in. Clean walkway surface. No paint residue.

tasks.name: Tool and Equipment Cleaning
tasks.description: Clean all brushes, spray equipment (flush lines, clean tip, filter), and tools. Proper cleaning of angled sash and flat brushes for reuse (~5,000 LF lifespan per brush). Flush airless sprayer with appropriate solvent (water for latex).

quality_notes.all: Full equipment clean. Brushes shaped and stored. Spray lines flushed.

sop_modules.sequence_notes: Final inspection -> Touch-up defects -> Glass unmask -> Threshold teardown -> Walkway teardown -> Tool cleaning.

round_configurations.description: 1 prime coat + 2 finish coats — standard NC sequence for bare substrates
2 finish coats only — factory-primed steel/fiberglass (adequate factory primer) or field-primed

applicability_rules.description: Steel-specific tasks activate only for steel substrate
Fiberglass-specific tasks activate only for fiberglass substrate
Wood-specific tasks activate only for wood substrate
Glass masking tasks activate for panel and grand_entry doors (doors with lites)
Panel recess brush tasks activate for panel and grand_entry complexity
Mullion/sidelite tasks activate only for grand_entry complexity
Spray equipment/tasks activate only for spray application method
Brush-only equipment/face tasks activate only for brush application method
Prime module skipped for factory-primed and field-primed substrates
Intercoat sanding is QT4/QT5 only — QT3 gets visual inspect only
Edge priming as separate task only when faces are sprayed (brush method covers edges in same pass)

exclusions.description: Door casing painting — belongs to SF_TRIM_EXT_NC_v1
exclusions.scope: Door casing prep, prime, and paint are NOT in this spec. This spec covers door slab, edges, frame/jamb, and glass lite masking only.
Casing-to-wall junction caulking is trim spec scope. This spec caulks panel joints on wood doors only.

exclusions.description: Roller application — not valid for exterior doors
exclusions.scope: Roller introduces orange peel on door faces. Only spray and brush are valid application methods. Back-rolling avoided on metal doors.

exclusions.description: Stain-grade fiberglass finishing — not NC paint scope
exclusions.scope: Stain-grade fiberglass doors requiring gel stain + clear topcoat are a different spec family. This spec covers paint-grade doors only.

exclusions.description: QT2 not applicable — exterior entry doors are architectural focal points
exclusions.scope: QT2 (basic) is excluded for exterior entry doors. Minimum quality tier is QT3.

assumptions.value: Panel doors with glass lites (half-lite, decorative glass) require glass masking. Single slab flush doors typically have no glass.
assumptions.note: Panel and grand_entry complexity tiers include glass lites by definition. Single_slab is flush with no glass. Masking tasks gate on door_complexity dimension.

assumptions.value: Panel joint caulking applies only to wood doors (steel/fiberglass panel joints are factory-sealed)
assumptions.note: Doctrine does not explicitly address steel/fiberglass panel joint caulking. Factory construction of steel and fiberglass doors seals panel joints during manufacturing. Wood doors with floating panels may develop gaps.

assumptions.value: Door must be propped open 24-48 hours after bottom edge painting to prevent seal sticking
assumptions.note: Doctrine mentions six-side seal but does not specify cure time for bottom edge. 24-48 hour prop time is standard industry practice for exterior door bottom edge coating cure.

assumptions.value: QT5 doors removed from hinges, painted in controlled environment (garage/shop), then re-hung for final coat with gravity leveling
assumptions.source: research.json RF-QT5; Exterior_Doors_Doctrine.md §7 (PCA Level 4 = cosmetic perfection)
assumptions.note: Doctrine defines PCA levels but does not explicitly state QT5 doors should be removed for controlled painting. This is derived from research and QT5 'supreme' standard requiring shop conditions.
